transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, thank you. I guess what finally pushed me to make the appointment is… I’ve been having trouble following through on things after audits or mentoring events. I’ll start the follow-up items with every intention of finishing them, and I really do mean to, but then a few days later I realize the final email, or a review note, or some form just never actually got done. It’s embarrassing, because I know I’m capable and I don’t want it to sound like I’m careless. I just keep finding these loose ends.
Do you often have trouble sustaining your attention on tasks, even when you want to focus?

Yes… I think so. I mean, not all the time, and I do try really hard to stay engaged. But in a long client meeting or even one of those AI-tool trainings, I’ll start out completely focused, taking it seriously, and then after a while I realize my mind has sort of slipped off. I’m still looking at the screen like I’m listening, but I’ve missed the last few minutes. It’s a little embarrassing to admit, because I don’t mean to tune out.
Looking back, did you have similar trouble paying attention or finishing tasks when you were a child?

Yes… I think so. I mean, I did well in school overall, so it wasn’t like anyone thought I couldn’t do the work. But I remember report cards saying things like I was bright, but I’d lose assignments or rush through and miss little details.  

I also apparently talked out of turn more than I’d like to admit, and teachers had to remind me to finish things. My mom still teases me that I could get an A on a test and then forget the project that was literally sitting in my backpack. Does that kind of thing count?
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about many different parts of your life, even when there isn’t a clear reason to?

I don’t think so… not excessively, anyway. I mean, I worry about normal things—work going well, whether I’ve forgotten something—but I wouldn’t say it’s many different parts of my life for no clear reason. At least, I haven’t really noticed it that way. Does that answer what you mean?
Do these attention and follow-through problems also happen outside of work, like at home or in daily life?

Yes… it does. I wish I could say it’s just work stress, but it kind of spills over.

At work, it’s gotten more noticeable than I’d like. I’ve made mistakes or left follow-up unfinished, and there was a client review that was affected by it. I’m trying to fix it, but I do worry people are starting to wonder if I can really handle the promotion.

And at home… my husband has had to take over some bills and commitments I said I’d handle, because I haven’t been reliable about finishing them. That’s hard to say, because I don’t want to sound irresponsible, but yes, it happens outside work too.
Do you find yourself repeatedly checking or redoing things because you feel driven to make them feel exactly right or to prevent something bad from happening?

Not really, no. I mean, I’ll double-check things sometimes, especially with work, because I don’t want to make a mistake—but I don’t feel like I’m driven to keep redoing it until it feels exactly right, or like something terrible will happen if I don’t.

At least, not in the way you’re describing, I don’t think. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Did these problems begin after a specific stressful event or major life change?

Not really after something bad happened, no. It was more after a big change at work… I got promoted after a firm-wide award, and the workload and responsibilities got a lot harder to juggle.

I’d say it’s been noticeably interfering for… maybe about a year and ten months now. I don’t want to make it sound like I just fell apart or anything, but that’s when it started becoming much harder to keep up. Does that make sense?
Have these attention and follow-through problems caused serious problems in your work or home life?

Yes… I think I have to say yes, even though I don’t like admitting that.

At work, it’s not just little slips anymore. Some mistakes and follow-up I didn’t finish affected a client review, and I’ve been worried people may be questioning whether I can really handle the promotion.

And at home, my husband has had to take over some bills and commitments that I said I would handle, because I haven’t been reliable about getting them done. I’m not proud of that, but yes… it has caused real problems.
